note: Korean P-CABs (tegoprazan, fexuprazan, revaprazan) reached GERD patients on dog acid-secretion and rat reflux-oesophagitis pharmacology; only tegoprazan's models were published, and both pointed the right way.
label: GERD (P-CABs)

engagement.model: Histamine- and pentagastrin-stimulated gastric acid secretion in dogs
engagement.note: Tegoprazan fully blocked histamine-stimulated acid secretion in dogs at 1 mg/kg within an hour.
engagement.quote: Tegoprazan potently inhibited histamine-induced gastric acid secretion in dogs, and a complete inhibition was observed at 1.0 mg/kg starting from 1 hour after administration.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Europe PMC); no full text.
engagement.judgement: First published use of the model for a member drug; the dog work predates the human phase 1 but its run date is unpublished, so the 2017 online date is the proxy.

engagement.model: Histamine- and pentagastrin-stimulated gastric acid secretion in dogs
engagement.note: In healthy men, tegoprazan raised 24-h intragastric pH quickly and dose-dependently, as the dog data predicted.
engagement.short: Rapid dose-dependent acid suppression in humans
engagement.quote: The pharmacodynamic analysis revealed that tegoprazan showed rapid, dose-dependent gastric acid suppression.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Han 2019 and Takahashi 2018; the pairing is mine.
engagement.reason: Human intragastric pH matched dog acid block
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Han 2019 does not set its pH data beside the dog data. Readout is acid (proximal) in both. Sunwoo 2020 (doi:10.1111/apt.16121) adds that tegoprazan 50 mg held pH>=4 for 54.5% of 24 h vs 25.1% for revaprazan 200 mg, so the weakest member engaged least; no published revaprazan or fexuprazan animal acid data were found, so they do not score here. Fexuprazan phase 1 (Sunwoo 2018, doi:10.1111/apt.14818) also showed rapid 24-h suppression.
engagement.magnitude_basis: onset and completeness of acid suppression (dog acid output vs human 24-h intragastric pH)

engagement.note: PBPK/PD model of tegoprazan built from in-vitro and clinical data to predict intragastric pH.
engagement.quote: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PBPK/PD) model for tegoprazan and its major metabolite M1 was developed to predict PK and PD profiles under various scenarios.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at first use; the comparison follows in the same paper.
engagement.model: SimCYP PBPK model of tegoprazan and M1 with an intragastric-pH PD model

engagement.note: Predicted 24-h pH>=4 holding 49.6% vs 48.9% observed (50 mg single); 63.0% vs 70.4% on day 7 at 100 mg.
engagement.quote: The percentage holding rates of pH ≥ 4 for 24 h after a single administration of 50 mg tegoprazan or repeated administrations of 100 mg tegoprazan for 7 days were similar to those of the clinical study.
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC9230797), Table 6. Observed data are Han 2019 healthy volunteers.
engagement.reason: Fitted to known human pH data
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction: the model was built and verified on tegoprazan healthy-volunteer PK/pH data published in 2019, so it reproduces, not predicts. Not used to choose a clinical dose.
engagement.magnitude_basis: predicted vs observed % time intragastric pH>=4 over 24 h
engagement.model: SimCYP PBPK model of tegoprazan and M1 with an intragastric-pH PD model

engagement.note: Fexuprazan PBPK model scaled from rat tissue partitioning and preclinical species; predicts exposure only, no pH.
engagement.quote: The extent of fexuprazan tissue distribution in humans was predicted using tissue-to-plasma partition coefficients in rats and the allometric relationships of fexuprazan distribution volumes (VSS) among preclinical species.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the PBPK model existed from 2021 but gave no acid readout until the 2022 PD extension.
engagement.model: Fexuprazan PBPK (rat partition coefficients, allometric scaling) and one-compartment PK models driving an intragastric-pH PD model

engagement.note: PK-PD models reproduced fexuprazan intragastric pH across 10-320 mg; 93-98% of points within 2-fold.
engagement.quote: Among the observed and simulated pH, the 93.4, 96.2, 98.3, and 98.3% data points were in the range of the two-fold difference or the >0.5 and <2× difference for Scenarios A, B, C, and D, respectively.
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC9230547). Observed pH from fexuprazan phase 1 healthy-volunteer studies.
engagement.reason: Fitted to known human pH data
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction: PD parameters were fitted to the published phase 1 pH data. The paper proposes a twice-daily regimen; no GERD trial of that regimen was found, so no dose entry.
engagement.magnitude_basis: simulated vs observed intragastric pH, fraction of points within 2-fold
engagement.model: Fexuprazan PBPK (rat partition coefficients, allometric scaling) and one-compartment PK models driving an intragastric-pH PD model

engagement.note: Platform predicts P-CAB PK and pH from chemical structure, calibrated on vonoprazan.
engagement.quote: Case studies are presented to assess and compare five potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB) compounds, after calibration and verification using vonoprazan and revaprazan.
engagement.model: AI-PBPK/PD platform (machine-learned ADME, calibrated on vonoprazan) predicting intragastric pH from structure

engagement.note: For revaprazan 200 mg it predicted 57.1% time at pH>4 vs 42.2% observed; onset 4 h predicted vs within 2 h observed.
engagement.quote: This was within a 1.5-fold variance from the study observation, which recorded a value of 42.2%
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC10904617). Observed side is Kim 2010 healthy male volunteers, cited by Wu, not re-read. Onset was over-predicted 2-fold; PK Cmax under-predicted ~2-fold.
engagement.reason: Revaprazan pH reproduced after the fact
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction: revaprazan's human pH data (2010) were public; revaprazan was the platform's verification compound. Within 2x on holding time, so retro, not contra, with source_calls_it match; onset and Cmax misses noted.
engagement.magnitude_basis: predicted vs observed % time intragastric pH>4 over 24 h, revaprazan 200 mg
engagement.model: AI-PBPK/PD platform (machine-learned ADME, calibrated on vonoprazan) predicting intragastric pH from structure

engagement.note: Cross-drug population PK/PD model fitted to published tegoprazan, fexuprazan, YH4808 and vonoprazan data.
engagement.quote: A multi-leveled population analysis was conducted using published pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic data on four representative PCABs: tegoprazan, YH4808, fexuprazan, and vonoprazan.
engagement.model: Semi-mechanistic multi-level population PK/PD model of P-CABs (food, circadian pH, pH-dependent absorption)

engagement.note: Predicted pH profiles and pH>4 holding times for tegoprazan and fexuprazan matched the healthy-volunteer data they were fitted to.
engagement.quote: Predicted pH profiles and holding times above pH 4 closely matched reported clinical outcomes.
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC12823312); per-drug predicted-vs-reported table not fully parsed from XML, so magnitude is direction_only.
engagement.reason: Fitted to known human pH data
engagement.judgement: Retrodiction: fitted to the same published phase 1 data it is compared with. 'Clinical outcomes' here are healthy-volunteer pH, not GERD healing.
engagement.magnitude_basis: predicted vs reported % time intragastric pH>4
engagement.model: Semi-mechanistic multi-level population PK/PD model of P-CABs (food, circadian pH, pH-dependent absorption)

dose.model: Histamine- and pentagastrin-stimulated gastric acid secretion in dogs
dose.note: Dogs needed 1-3 mg/kg for full acid block; nobody compared that with the 50 mg human dose, which clinical dose-ranging set.
dose.short: Dog mg/kg never compared with human dose
dose.quote: Moreover, an oral administration of tegoprazan at 1 and 3 mg/kg reversed the pentagastrin-induced acidified gastric pH to the neutral range.
dose.judgement: Untested, not same: the model gave an oral mg/kg, not an exposure target, and no source translates it. Human 50 mg (~0.7 mg/kg) worked, but the phase 2 dose-ranging healed 96-98% at 50-200 mg (cited in Lee 2019, PMC6594096), i.e. the dose came from patients. Rat GERD ED50 2.0 mg/kg (Kim 2019) likewise uncompared. Fexuprazan's PBPK model (Jeong 2021, doi:10.3390/pharmaceutics13060813) scaled rat and preclinical-species data to human PK, but it was built after human PK was known and predicts exposure, not an effective target, so it is not scored.

efficacy.model: Rat reflux-oesophagitis model (esophageal injury and acid secretion), vs esomeprazole
efficacy.note: Tegoprazan dose-dependently prevented reflux injury in rats, 15-fold more potently than esomeprazole.
efficacy.quote: In a GERD model, tegoprazan showed dose-dependent efficacy in inhibiting esophageal injury and gastric acid secretion with an ED50 of 2.0 mg/kg, which was 15-fold more potent than that of esomeprazole.
efficacy.judgement: Only published reflux-disease model for any member drug. Published two weeks after the Korean phase 3 and after the 2018 Korean approval; treated as prospective pharmacology published late, not a retrodiction, because development-stage rat efficacy work precedes phase 3 by convention, but its run date is unpublished.

efficacy.model: Rat reflux-oesophagitis model (esophageal injury and acid secretion), vs esomeprazole
efficacy.note: Tegoprazan healed erosive oesophagitis as well as esomeprazole (98.9% each at 8 weeks); the rat potency edge did not show at this ceiling.
efficacy.short: Tegoprazan heals EE, non-inferior to esomeprazole
efficacy.quote: The cumulative healing rates at week 8 were 98.9% (91/92), 98.9% (90/91) and 98.9% (87/88) for tegoprazan 50 mg, tegoprazan 100 mg and esomeprazole 40 mg, respectively.
efficacy.confidence_note: Lee 2019 full text read (PMC6594096); Kim 2019 abstract only.
efficacy.reason: EE healed as rat model predicted
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: Lee 2019 cites unnamed 'nonclinical studies' of faster, more potent acid suppression, which is a citation, not a comparison. Primary endpoint (non-inferior healing by week 8) met, so same, direction only. The rat model's implied superiority over a PPI was not visible in Korea (ceiling ~99% in all arms) but later appeared in the US TRIUMpH-EE trial against lansoprazole (see patient_trials); I did not add a second same entry because it changes no status. Fexuprazan healed EE non-inferior to esomeprazole without any published animal model. Revaprazan has no GERD efficacy trial found (Korean approval is for ulcer and gastritis).
efficacy.magnitude_basis: erosive oesophagitis healing (rat injury inhibition vs endoscopic healing at week 8)

patient_trials.quote: Both doses of tegoprazan were non-inferior to esomeprazole 40 mg.
Fexuprazan was non-inferior to esomeprazole regarding the healing rate at week 8 [99.1% (106/107) vs 99.1% (110/111)].
Tegoprazan met the primary endpoint, demonstrating non-inferiority to lansoprazole for complete healing by week 8 in all patients (84.6% vs 78.0%, p<0.0001).

safety.model: Rat 1-4 week repeat dosing: gastrin, gastric emptying, small-intestinal microbiota
safety.note: Rats on tegoprazan had raised gastrin and transient slow emptying, like esomeprazole; no patient comparison of long-term harms yet.
safety.short: Rat gastrin rise like PPI; uncompared
safety.quote: Therefore, the acid suppression-related adverse effects of P-CABs and PPIs are expected to be similar.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The rodent toxicology and carcinogenicity package filed in Korea for tegoprazan and fexuprazan is not public.
safety.judgement: The only published member-drug animal safety data. Gastrin rise is a mechanism marker, not a harm, so human gastrin data (fexuprazan vs esomeprazole no different, Lee 2022; TRIUMpH gastrin within normal range, Sebela press release 2025) do not score it. Phase 3 trials report AEs comparable to PPIs over 8 weeks; long-term ECL/NET outcomes for members are unreported.
